start.topic: Perimeter of rectangles, squares and polygons
start.opening: Namaste Kabir, main Asha, aapki AI teacher hoon. Aaj perimeter seekhenge. Aapko maths mein kaunsa topic achchha lagta hai?

turns.line: rectangle ke chaaron sides jodenge, 50 plus 30 plus 50 plus 30, 160 metre
turns.reply: Kabir, aapne rectangle ki chaaron sides jodkar sahi method lagaya. Ab bataiye, yeh boundary naapna perimeter kehlaayega ya area?
Aage badhiye—formula ko poora kijiye, phir 50 aur 30 ki jagah rakhkar perimeter nikaaliye.
Theek hai, ab square: uski chaaron sides barabar hoti hain, isliye perimeter nikaalne ke liye side ko 4 se guna kijiye. Side 6 metre ho toh?

record.summary:
Kabir practised finding rectangle perimeter by adding all four sides.
Kabir calculated 50 + 30 + 50 + 30 as 160 metres.
Kabir stated the shortcut as 2 × length + breadth, missing brackets around length and breadth.
No later corrected statement was recorded.
record.parentNote: Kabir practised finding a rectangle’s perimeter by adding its four sides and obtained 160 metres for sides 50 m and 30 m. Kabir also tried the shortcut but left out the brackets: the correct form is 2 × (length + breadth), and this mix-up was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, Kabir can write both methods for a few rectangles and check that they give the same answer.
